content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are working in the inkling repo (Electron + React + TypeScript + SQLite, Windows app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root first and follow it (docs rules, PR rules, the "three ways to hurt yourself", no repo-wide checks). Do the work yourself; do not start subagents.

## Goal
The "Where code lives" section of AGENTS.md is stale and sends agents to the wrong files. Fix it with the smallest accurate edit. Docs-only change.

## Known problems (verify each against the code before writing; do not trust this list blindly)
1. The `src/components/` bullet says "The library grid, cards, and Spaces UI live in `src/App.tsx`, and the reader is `src/ReaderView.tsx`." In reality the app is organised by feature under `src/features/` (capture, item-view, library, settings, shell, spaces). The library grid/cards are in `src/features/library/` (e.g. LibraryStage.tsx, LibraryCard.tsx), the expanded item overlay and PDF viewer are in `src/features/item-view/`, Spaces logic is in `src/features/spaces/` plus `src/features/shell/SpacesSection.tsx`. `src/App.tsx` is only the top-level wiring of those features. `src/components/` holds shared pieces (ItemMedia.tsx, LiquidGlass, mascot, onboarding, etc.). `src/ReaderView.tsx` still exists; confirm.
2. The section omits places an agent needs to know about: `packages/contracts` (the IPC command list and Effect Schemas shared by preload, main and renderer; see docs/tech-stack.md), `packages/ingestion-shared`, `extension/` (the browser extension, itself a capture entry point), `scripts/`, and `electron/storage/` (SQLite storage and job queue; confirm the layout). Check `src/lib/`, `src/ui/` too and mention only what is useful.
3. Check every other path named in the "Where code lives" section still exists and is described accurately (`src/lib/ingestion/`, `benchmarks/`, `public/seed-demo/`, `src/seedPersonal.ts`, `docs/`, `oxlint-plugin-inkling/` if mentioned). Fix anything else that is wrong.

## Constraints
- Edit only the "Where code lives" section of AGENTS.md unless you find another factually wrong path reference elsewhere in the file; then fix that too and say so in the PR.
- Keep it short: one line per location, no file catalogs, no enumerating every file. The AGENTS.md documentation rules apply: add only what a maintainer/agent would get wrong without it. Match the existing voice and formatting.
- Do not touch docs/changelog.md (trivial doc fix; AGENTS.md says trivial edits skip the changelog). Never mention an agent did the work in docs.
- Do not start dev servers or the Electron app. No full test/typecheck runs. Verify by reading the repo (ls, grep) that every path you wrote exists. `bun run check:refs` (scripts/assert-command-refs.ts) validates command references in docs; run it if it is cheap and relevant.
- Create a branch from the current HEAD named `docs/agents-code-map` (you are in your own worktree).

## Delivery (full-stop: PR ready for the user to merge, but you NEVER merge)
- Commit with a conventional title, e.g. `docs(agents): correct the code map in AGENTS.md`. End the commit message with the line: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Fetch origin, rebase onto the latest origin/main, push the branch, and open a PR with `gh` (use the `file-pr` skill if you have it). PR body: the problem in a sentence or two (stale paths in the code map), then what you changed, one short line saying how you verified (every path checked on disk). End the body with: `Claude Haiku 5.5 (T3 Code)` and then `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- Never merge, enable auto-merge, enter a merge queue, push to main, or bypass protections. Do not call watch_pull_request. If checks run (CI skips docs-only pushes by design), look once at their state and report it; do not poll or sleep.
- If a bot or CI finding appears while you are still active, fix real ones and push; otherwise just report state.
- Your final message's last line must be exactly: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`. Before it, list in 3-6 lines what you changed and anything you were unsure about.
I'll start by checking the worktree state and locating the "Where code lives" section.

155	The Electron main process owns files, the job queue, the database, and model execution. The renderer gets a narrow preload bridge, not raw filesystem or shell access. Fetched HTML is untrusted. It gets sanitized, embeds pass an allowlist, scripts and event handlers are stripped.
156	
157	Full reasoning in `docs/tech-stack.md`. Behavior contract in `docs/product-behavior.md`.
158	
159	## Where code lives
160	
161	- `src/` is the React and TypeScript frontend. Entry at `src/main.tsx`.
162	- `src/lib/ingestion/` is the capture and extraction pipeline. Defuddle, metadata fallback, sanitizing, video link handling.
163	- `src/components/` holds shared pieces such as the card media (`ItemMedia.tsx`), the expanded item overlay, and the PDF viewer. The library grid, cards, and Spaces UI live in `src/App.tsx`, and the reader is `src/ReaderView.tsx`.
164	- `electron/` holds the desktop main process, preload bridge, SQLite storage, job queue, PDF/OCR, embeddings, and packaging inputs.
165	- `benchmarks/` holds the 48 item corpus, the harness, expected outputs, and results. Of the results, only `results-latest.json` and `summary.md` are tracked.
166	- `public/seed-demo/` plus `src/seedPersonal.ts` is the committed demo library for UI work.
167	- `docs/` holds product, behavior, stack, roadmap, and changelog. No other docs home exists yet.
168	
169	## Taste
170	
171	- Complexity belongs at the adapter boundary. Ingestion stays explicit, UI stays dumb.
172	- Inferred types over annotations. `any` is the enemy.
173	- Default to no comment. Keep one only where a reader would likely break something without it: a race or ordering guarantee, a security or sanitizing check, a Chromium, Electron, WebGPU or OS quirk, or an invariant another file relies on. One line where you can, four at most. Don't restate names, narrate steps, label sections, record history, explain the fix you just made (the PR carries that), or leave a TODO without an issue. Lint directives, knip tags and license headers stay. `inkling/no-low-value-comments` in `oxlint-plugin-inkling/` enforces the length cap and the mechanical cases, and every `oxlint-disable` needs a `-- reason`.
174	- Our users should never notice a dropped frame, a lying spinner, and a stale label. No continuously repainting animations(with a slight execption for the mascot); they peg the GPU on high-refresh displays.

--- extension README head
# Save to inkling from Chrome

Click the inkling toolbar icon to save the current page URL. You can also right-click a link or the page and choose **Save to inkling**. The extension sends the URL and its title; inkling handles extraction and processing in the background.

## Connect the local receiver

Pairing is optional. When the extension has the app's receiver address and token, it posts to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/captures` with the bearer token from inkling's **Settings → Extension** panel. The server chooses an available loopback port when inkling starts, so update the address in the extension's options if that port changes. The token stays in this browser profile and is sent only to `127.0.0.1`.

Without pairing, or if the receiver is unavailable, the extension hands the URL to the app through the existing `inkling://capture?url=...` link. Both paths use inkling's existing URL-capture behavior; the extension does not read page content or contact a remote service.

To pair, open the extension's **Details → Extension options**, copy the listening address and pairing token from inkling's **Settings → Extension**, and save them there. If inkling is not running, the capture link can start it when the operating system has registered the `inkling://` protocol.

## Load unpacked

1. Install the repository dependencies with `bun install`.
2. Build the extension from the repository root: `bun run --cwd extension build`.
3. In Chrome, open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**, choose **Load unpacked**, and select `extension/dist/`.

The manifest grants access to the active tab only after a save action. Its loopback host permission is limited to `127.0.0.1`; there are no persistent page scripts or broad website permissions.

--- lib/ingestion README head
# Ingestion utilities

These modules are pure, UI-independent building blocks for the local ingestion
pipeline.

- `file-classification.ts` classifies a File-like value as `image`, `pdf`,
  `video`, or `other`, using MIME type first and the filename extension as a
  fallback.
- `asset-paths.ts` provides the deterministic thumbnail policy and safe,
  app-relative asset paths. Generated previews are `webp` for images/videos and
  `png` for the first PDF page; other files do not get a generated thumbnail.
- `safe-embeds.ts` canonicalizes YouTube and Vimeo URLs to fixed provider
  origins. Direct video files require an exact HTTPS origin in
  `allowedDirectMediaOrigins`. `javascript:`, `data:`, `blob:`, HTTP, URLs with
  credentials/ports, unknown hosts, and malformed provider URLs are rejected.
- `x-post.ts` recognizes public X/Twitter Post URLs and normalizes the official
  X oEmbed response into sanitized embed markup plus searchable post metadata.
  URL ingestion persists that metadata under `social`; the UI upgrades it with
  X's official widgets when available and keeps a local fallback for offline or
  blocked embeds.

No function in this folder fetches network content, executes embeds, performs
OCR, or exposes AI-derived metadata. A later ingestion service can call these
helpers after Defuddle/Tesseract extraction and before persisting local assets.
